newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican labor boss says vote PRI or get out of union.
newsitem.headline: Mexican labor boss says vote PRI or get out of union.

text.p: The boss of Mexico's main labour union has left little doubt where he stands ahead of key mid-term elections in July: vote for the ruling party or get out, he told his six million members.

Seeking to counter a rising tide of opposition to the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI), Fidel Velazquez, the 96-year-old leader of the Confederation of Mexican Workers (CTM), went on the attack this week.
"Our comrades have not understood up to now that voting for another party that is not the PRI sometimes helps our enemies to win," he told a CTM general assembly on Tuesday evening.
"Neither traitors nor cowards have a place in the CTM, and if we end up with a reduced number of comrades, we would prefer that," he said, his frail voice cracking with anger.
"Whoever doesn't agree, go home! There's no room for you in the CTM," he said.
Velazquez's broadside followed what he said was the failure of many CTM mebers to vote for the PRI in local elections in the State of Mexico last November.

This year, the PRI, which has ruled Mexico for nearly 68 years -- partly because of its robust support among unions -- faces a tough contest in a race to renew the chamber of deputies and select the first elected mayor of Mexico City.
Though the party has sought to present a more democratic face, Velazquez showed it was continuing to rely on old-style intimidation tactics to muster support in some quarters.

Velazquez's own democratic credentials have been widely questioned. On Tuesday, he was named to head the CTM until 2004, which would take him beyond his 100th birthday. The vote was unanimous and no candidate opposed him.
